current_route.title: HfO2/SiO2 Dichroic Stack with Hybrid Thickness Initialization
current_route.scientific_hypothesis: A hybrid initialization scheme combining 60% QWOT-centered candidates with 40% harmonic half/double-multiple thickness candidates, plus ±5nm noise injection in the first optimization step, will produce higher best_target_score and maintain tightest_margin compared to pure QWOT±10% initialization across iteration rounds.
current_route.design_principle: Quarter-wave optical thickness (QWOT) stacks create constructive interference for reflection at design wavelengths. For a dichroic filter blocking 400-700nm while passing 1530-1565nm, the high-index HfO2 and low-index SiO2 layers should have optical thicknesses near λ/4 at a center wavelength in the visible blocking band. However, pure QWOT initialization creates symmetry that can trap gradient-based optimizers; harmonic perturbations (λ/8, λ/2 multiples) break this symmetry while remaining physically meaningful.
